ev.y_bulla.text: On your {g:ninth|eighth} day you were purified, named and given a {g:bulla, a little amulet pouch,|lunula, a crescent-moon charm,} to wear around your neck. It will guard you from the evil eye until you come of age.
ev.y_amphidromia.text: On your fifth day you were carried at a run around the household hearth: that is how Athenians welcome a newborn into the family. {npc}, your father, hung {g:an olive branch|a tuft of wool} on the door himself so the neighbors would know who had been born.
ev.y_nile_lullaby.text: {npc}, your mother, sang you a lullaby about the Nile flood and kept the flies off you all night with a fan of palm leaves.
ev.y_first_word.text.1: Your first word was the name of the neighbors' dog. Your parents pretended not to be offended.
ev.y_first_word.text.2: You stood up for the first time and tottered straight toward the porridge bowl. Your mother caught you at the last moment.
ev.y_first_word.text.3: Your first tooth came through, and you put it to use at once — on your grandfather's finger. He laughed and swore at the same time.
ev.y_choes.text: At the spring festival of the Anthesteria you, like the other little ones, were given a tiny painted jug and a wreath of flowers. You carried the jug around all day and wouldn't let anyone touch it.
ev.y_wooden_toy.text: Grandfather carved you {g:a little wooden horse on wheels|a wooden doll with jointed arms}. Now you sleep hugging it and drag it everywhere all day.
ev.y_sacred_cat.text: You pulled the neighbors' cat by the tail, and your mother went pale. All evening she explained: the cat is the creature of the goddess Bastet, and harming one brings great misfortune.
ev.y_grandma_tales.text: By the fire Grandmother told frightening and wonderful stories of gods and heroes. You always fell asleep before the end and demanded the rest in the morning.
ev.y_grandma_tales.text.rome: By the fire Grandmother told the story of the twins Romulus and Remus, nursed by a she-wolf. Ever since, you have looked at every dog with respect.
ev.y_grandma_tales.text.athens: By the fire Grandmother told how Theseus slew the Minotaur and found his way out of the labyrinth by a thread. The next day you wandered the courtyard with a ball of wool.
ev.y_grandma_tales.text.egypt: By the fire Grandmother told how Isis searched the whole land for her husband Osiris and brought him back to life. You cried, even though you knew it would end well.
ev.y_saturnalia_kid.text: For the Saturnalia you were given little clay figurines and allowed to play at nuts until late at night. The whole house feasted and shouted, and nobody scolded anyone.
ev.y_scolding.text.1: {npc}, your mother, found you standing over a smashed jar of oil. You swore it fell by itself, but the oily footprints led straight to you.
ev.y_scolding.text.2: {npc}, your mother, baked honey cakes for the guests. By the time the guests arrived there were three fewer, and your cheeks were mysteriously sticky.
ev.y_storm_sibling.text: A thunderstorm raged all night. Your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister} {npc} crawled under your blanket, and until morning you argued in whispers about who had made the Thunderer so angry.
ev.y_goat_kid.text: The goat had twins, and the weakest kid was given to you to raise. Now it follows you everywhere and chews the hem of your tunic.
ev.y_master_son_nuts.text: While no one was looking, you played at nuts with the master's son. He lost and didn't even mind — then his nurse came and led him away without a glance at you.
ev.y_first_baths.text: You were taken to the public baths for the first time: hot water, echoing vaults, pastry sellers shouting — and strict orders not to jump into the cold pool. Of course you jumped.
ev.y_hungry_winter.text: It was a hungry winter. Mother divided each flatbread so that nothing was left for herself, and you learned to fall asleep without thinking about food.
ev.y_knucklebones.text: You won a whole handful of knucklebones from the neighborhood kids. The secret is simple: throw with a twist and hold your breath.
ev.y_knucklebones.text.rome: You won a whole handful of knucklebones from the neighborhood kids. You rolled the Venus throw — all four showing different sides! — and even the older boys came over to look.
ev.y_hoop.text: You were driving a bronze hoop with jingling rings down the street and knocked over a basket of figs at the corner. The fruit seller chased you for two blocks.
ev.y_scare_birds.text: Before dawn you were sent out to the field with a clapper to chase the birds off the seed. By noon you were hoarse, but the crows seemed to respect you.
ev.y_fly_whisk.text: You were set to stand by the master's table and wave the flies away with a fan. You had to stand still and silent, and the smell of roast meat made your stomach ache.
ev.y_potter_father.text: {npc}, your father, sat you down at the potter's wheel. Your bowl came out as lopsided as a drunken satyr, but he fired it in the kiln anyway and put it on the shelf.
ev.y_acropolis.text: {npc}, your father, took you up to the Acropolis for the first time. The marble was blinding, and in the dimness of the temple towered a huge Athena of gold and ivory.
ev.y_first_sea.text: You saw the sea for the first time. It was huge and salty and simply never ended.
ev.y_first_sea.text.rome: You were taken to Ostia for the first time and saw the sea — and the ships bringing grain to Rome from all over the world. You kept tasting the water all day: it really is salty.
ev.y_first_sea.text.athens: You were taken down to the Piraeus for the first time: a forest of masts, shouting porters, the smell of pitch and fish — and the sea stretching to the edge of the sky.
ev.y_army_passes.text: An army marched past your house: helmets flashing, trumpets blaring, standards swaying above the ranks. You ran after it until your feet were sore.
ev.y_inundation.text: The Nile flooded, and the village became a scatter of little islands. Neighbors visit each other in papyrus boats, and you fish straight from the doorstep.
ev.y_barque_procession.text: Priests carried the god's sacred barque with its closed shrine through the streets. You squeezed into the front row and tried to peek inside, but saw only incense smoke.
ev.y_pharos.text: You sailed into Alexandria after dark, and above the sea burned the fire of the Pharos — a lighthouse taller than any temple. You stayed on deck until morning.
ev.y_crocodile.text: By the canal one of the children screamed: a crocodile was lying in the reeds. You ran all the way to the village without looking back, and only at home noticed you'd lost a sandal.
ev.y_lost_tooth.text: You lost a tooth. The boy next door said to throw it onto the roof; Grandmother said to bury it by the threshold. Just in case, you hid it in a crack in the wall.
ev.y_swim.text: On a hot day you swam on your own for the first time — doggy-paddling, eyes bulging, but swimming!
ev.y_swim.text.rome: On a hot day you swam across a backwater of the Tiber for the first time. Father says a Roman must know how to swim — how else will he cross rivers on campaign?
ev.y_swim.text.athens: On a hot day you swam on your own for the first time. In Athens they say of a dunce, 'He can neither swim nor read' — so you're halfway there.
ev.y_swim.text.egypt: On a hot day you swam in an irrigation canal for the first time, while the grown-ups kept a sharp eye on the reeds. Crocodiles are no joke.
ev.y_pyramids.text: {npc}, your father, took you on a barge sailing down the Nile. At sunset the pyramids rose at the edge of the desert — so ancient that even the old folk only tell fairy tales about them.
ev.y_nickname.text.1: The neighborhood kids nicknamed you Chick, for your skinny legs. You were angry for exactly a week, then got used to it.
ev.y_nickname.text.2: For your love of boiled chickpeas they started calling you Chickpea. You don't mind: chickpeas are a fine thing.
ev.y_nickname.text.3: They call you Owl: you're the only one who stays awake when the grown-ups tell scary stories. The owl is a wise bird, you decided.
ev.y_olive_harvest.text: In late autumn the whole household gathered olives: the adults beat the branches with sticks, and the children crawled along the ground with baskets. By evening your back ached and your fingers were black with juice.
ev.y_false_coin.text: {npc}, your father, showed you how to spot a fake coin: ring it on the counter and nick the edge — thin silver can hide copper underneath.
ev.y_pedagogue.text: Every morning an old slave tutor walks you to school carrying your writing tablets. You like his stories on the way far better than the teacher's lessons.
ev.y_father_scar.text: {npc}, your father, showed you an old scar on his shoulder and told you about the campaign where he got it. The story changes a little every time, but you still listen breathlessly.
ev.y_spindle.text: {npc}, your mother, taught you to spin: spindle in your hand, distaff under your arm. The thread broke twenty times, but by evening it was coming out even.
ev.y_friend_hideout.text: Your friend {npc} showed you a hiding place behind an old tomb by the road. Your treasures are kept there now: a shiny potsherd, a bird's feather and a dried lizard.
ev.y_friend_race.text: Your friend {npc} challenged you to a race to the old tree. You arrived neck and neck and argued until you were hoarse about who won.
ev.y_sibling_lamp.text: Your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister} {npc} broke a clay lamp and blamed it all on you. But that evening {g=npc_sex:he|she} secretly brought you half {g=npc_sex:his|her} flatbread to make peace.
ev.y_wax_tablet.text: You scratched letters into a wax tablet with a stylus while the teacher paced between the benches with his cane. At least you can rub out a mistake with the blunt end — unlike in life.
ev.y_two_tongues.text: At home everyone speaks Egyptian, but the scribes and tax men at the market speak Greek. You've learned 'hello' and 'how much?' in both languages and are very proud of it.
ev.y_market_errand.text: For the first time you were sent to the market alone with money. You counted the change three times and even haggled down the price of onions.
ev.y_palaestra.text: The palaestra smells of olive oil and dust. The wrestling master throws you onto the sand again and again, and afterward you scrape yourself clean with a strigil like a real athlete.
ev.y_full_sack.text: For the first time you lifted a full sack of grain and carried it to the cart without help. The grown-ups exchanged looks: a real worker is growing up.
ev.y_roof_stars.text: One stifling night you climbed onto the flat roof and watched the stars until dawn, wondering what your life would be like. The stars gave no answer, but your heart felt calmer.
ev.y_koureion.text: At the festival of the Apatouria you cut your hair and dedicated it to the gods, and {npc}, your father, presented you to the men of his phratry and swore you were his lawful son. Now you belong to the clan and the city.
ev.y_stray_dog.title: A puppy in the rain
ev.y_stray_dog.text: A soaked puppy shivers under an awning — skinny, with one floppy ear. It looks at you as if it had been waiting for you all along.
ev.y_stray_dog.take_home: Take it home and beg your parents
ev.y_stray_dog.take_home.success: Father grumbled but gave in. You have a dog!
ev.y_stray_dog.take_home.failure: 'Another mouth to feed?' Father put the puppy out the door. You cried all evening.
ev.y_dog_saves.title: The old dog
ev.y_dog_saves.text: The dog you once fed as a puppy has gone grey around the muzzle. Tonight he suddenly started barking furiously: someone is breaking into the storeroom.
ev.y_dog_saves.chase: Charge the thieves with the dog
ev.y_dog_saves.chase.success: The thieves fled, dropping a sack. By morning the whole street is talking about you and your dog.
ev.y_dog_saves.chase.failure: One of the thieves managed to club you. The goods were saved, but your head rang for a week.
ev.y_dog_saves.wake: Wake the neighbors with a shout
ev.y_friend_caught.title: Caught by the ear
ev.y_friend_caught.text: Your friend {npc} snatched a honey cake from a stall and ran off, and the vendor grabbed you by the ear instead. 'Who stole it? Talk, or we're going to your father!'
ev.y_friend_caught.name: Name your friend
ev.y_friend_caught.wriggle.success: You left the vendor holding a scrap of your tunic and vanished down an alley.
ev.y_friend_caught.wriggle.failure: The vendor held on tight. Your father had to pay for the cake and blush.
ev.y_friend_repays.title: An old debt
ev.y_friend_repays.text: {npc}, the friend you once took the blame for at the honey-cake stall, has done well in life. {g=npc_sex:He|She} sought you out: 'I haven't forgotten. Let me repay the debt.'
ev.y_friend_grudge.title: A childhood grudge
ev.y_friend_grudge.text: {npc} never forgave you for the honey-cake vendor. Now {g=npc_sex:he|she} tells the story to everyone you both know — and every time you come off worse.
ev.y_friend_grudge.apologize.success: You talked until nightfall and laughed together for the first time in years.
ev.y_friend_grudge.apologize.failure: 'Too late,' you heard, and the door closed.
ev.y_runaway_secret.title: Someone else's secret
ev.y_runaway_secret.text: Every night the woman next door carries bread to an abandoned shed. You peeked: a runaway slave is hiding there, hardly more than a boy. Sheltering runaways is punished harshly — and so is knowing about it.
ev.y_runaway_secret.bring_food.success: Nobody noticed. A week later the shed was empty — he had slipped away in the night.
ev.y_runaway_secret.bring_food.failure: Mother noticed the missing bread and got the truth out of you. There was a hard conversation at home.
ev.y_runaway_thanks.title: A stranger at the harbor
ev.y_runaway_thanks.text: At the harbor a weather-beaten man came up to you. 'Don't you know me? The shed, the bread, the night. You didn't give me away. I got out — and now I sail on ships, far from here, where no one is looking for me.'
ev.y_runaway_thanks.friendship: Invite him for a cup of wine
ev.y_runaway_fate.title: The millstones
ev.y_runaway_fate.text: At the market you happened to learn what became of the runaway from the neighbor's shed: he was returned to his master and has been turning millstones ever since.
ev.y_runaway_fate.pray: Light a lamp for him at the altar
ev.y_runaway_fate.seek: Find him and slip him your savings
ev.y_toga_virilis.title: The toga of manhood
ev.y_toga_virilis.text: On the feast of the Liberalia you took off your childhood bulla and left it at the altar of the household gods. Father draped the white toga of manhood over you and led you to the Forum. You're a citizen now — where will you begin?
ev.y_toga_virilis.note: Around the age of 14–16 a Roman boy set aside the purple-bordered toga of childhood and his bulla amulet and put on the plain white toga virilis. The ceremony was often held at the Liberalia on 17 March. Afterwards youths of good family served an 'apprenticeship of the Forum' under an experienced orator, while the Campus Martius was the place for weapons training.
ev.y_toga_virilis.forum: Haunt the Forum and learn from the orators
ev.y_toga_virilis.campus: Train with weapons on the Field of Mars
ev.y_ephebeia.title: The ephebe's oath
ev.y_ephebeia.text: You are eighteen — an ephebe. In the sanctuary of Aglauros you swear never to shame the sacred weapons and never to desert your comrade in the line. Ahead lies service in the border forts of Attica.
ev.y_ephebeia.note: From the 330s BC Athenian citizen youths aged 18–20 served as ephebes: they swore an oath in the sanctuary of Aglauros, trained for war and garrisoned the border forts. Later the ephebeia became voluntary, lasted a single year and turned into a kind of school for well-off young men, who also attended philosophers' lectures.
ev.y_ephebeia.garrison: Stand watch faithfully on the frontier
ev.y_ephebeia.torch: Aim to be the best — run in the torch relay
ev.y_ephebeia.torch.success: Your team finished first with the torch still alight. The whole company cheers you.
ev.y_ephebeia.torch.failure: On the last lap the torch went out in your hand. They laughed for a long time.
ev.y_ephebeia.lectures: Serve your time and attend the philosophers
ev.y_ephebe_comrade.title: A comrade from the watch
ev.y_ephebe_comrade.text: A comrade from your ephebe days, with whom you once froze on watch on a fortress wall, has sought you out. He is fitting out a ship with olive oil for the Black Sea and needs a partner he can trust — like back then, on the wall.
ev.y_ephebe_comrade.join.success: The ship came back laden with grain and profit. The old friendship paid off.
ev.y_ephebe_comrade.join.failure: The ship ran into a storm and was lost. Your money went down with it.
ev.y_ephebe_comrade.decline: Decline — the sea can't be trusted
ev.y_poll_tax_list.title: On the tax roll
ev.y_poll_tax_list.text: You're fourteen, and the village scribe has entered your name on the poll-tax roll: as far as the treasury is concerned, you're a man now. Wiping his reed pen, the scribe eyes you: 'Sharp lad. Know your letters?'
ev.y_poll_tax_list.note: In Roman Egypt men aged roughly 14 to 62 paid a poll tax, the laographia. A house-by-house census was taken every 14 years, and scribes kept name-by-name lists of taxpayers in every village.
ev.y_poll_tax_list.ask_scribe.success: The scribe grunted and handed you a potsherd to practice on. Now you learn your letters every evening.
ev.y_poll_tax_list.ask_scribe.failure: 'First learn to hold your tongue,' said the scribe, waving you off.
ev.y_poll_tax_list.field: Back to the field — the tax won't pay itself
ev.y_scribe_job.title: The scribe's post
ev.y_scribe_job.text: The old scribe who once taught you your letters is going blind. He asks you to keep the village tax rolls for him: 'Your hand is steady. Your conscience — we'll see.'
ev.y_scribe_job.take: Take up the pen and the rolls
ev.y_girl_dedication.title: A doll for the goddess
ev.y_girl_dedication.text: You'll be married soon, and by custom a girl leaves her toys to the goddess before her wedding. Mother reminds you: it's time to take your old doll with the chipped nose to the temple.
ev.y_girl_dedication.dedicate: Take the doll to the temple
ev.y_girl_dedication.keep: Hide the doll in your dowry chest
ev.y_girl_dedication.give: Give it to the little girl next door
ev.y_cheat_school.title: Learned by heart
ev.y_cheat_school.text: Tomorrow the teacher will make you recite a long passage by heart, and you haven't learned half of it. Your benchmate offers to prompt you for a handful of nuts.
ev.y_cheat_school.text.rome: Tomorrow the teacher will make you recite the Twelve Tables by heart, and you haven't learned half of them. Your benchmate offers to prompt you for a handful of nuts.
ev.y_cheat_school.text.athens: Tomorrow the teacher will make you recite a book of the Iliad by heart, and you haven't learned half of it. Your benchmate offers to prompt you for a handful of nuts.
ev.y_cheat_school.text.egypt: Tomorrow the teacher will give a dictation of Greek maxims, and you haven't learned half of them. Your benchmate offers to prompt you for a handful of dates.
ev.y_cheat_school.cheat.success: You rattled it all off without a stumble. The teacher even praised you — which feels a little shameful.
ev.y_cheat_school.cheat.failure: The teacher heard the whispering. You both got it, and at home you got it again from your father.
ev.y_cheat_school.confess.success: The teacher grunted, 'Honesty is a lesson too,' and gave you another day.
ev.y_cheat_school.confess.failure: The teacher did not appreciate honesty and reached for the cane.
ev.y_procession_run.title: The procession
ev.y_procession_run.text: A festival procession is passing through the whole city, and all the neighborhood kids are already there. And you've been told to stay home and sort lentils.
ev.y_procession_run.text.rome: Today a triumphing general rides along the Sacred Way: a golden chariot, captives, wagons of plunder, soldiers singing cheeky songs. And you've been told to stay home and sort lentils.
ev.y_procession_run.text.athens: Today the statue of Dionysus is brought into the city in procession: pipes, masked revelers, bulls for sacrifice, and theatre afterwards. And you've been told to stay home and sort lentils.
ev.y_procession_run.text.egypt: Today the goddess's barque is carried to the temple: rattling sistrums, pipes, free bread and beer. And you've been told to stay home and sort lentils.
ev.y_procession_run.sneak.success: You saw everything from the shoulders of a kind porter and got home before your mother.
ev.y_procession_run.sneak.failure: You got lost in the crowd and searched for the way home until evening. Mother had already run up and down the whole street.
ev.y_procession_run.with_sibling: Sneak out with your brother or sister
ev.y_first_job.title: First job
ev.y_first_job.text: The neighbors are looking for someone to do odd jobs for a couple of coins a day. There are two offers, and each one smells in its own way.
ev.y_first_job.fuller: At the fuller's — tread wool in the vats
ev.y_first_job.baker: At the baker's — deliver bread before dawn
ev.y_first_job.play: Stay a child a little longer
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.title: The broken amphora
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.text: The amphora of oil lies in pieces. Father asks who did it, and {npc} silently looks at you. You both knocked it over, fighting for the last fig.
ev.y_sibling_quarrel.blame: Put it all on the other one
ev.y_sibling_remembers.title: Family dinner
ev.y_sibling_remembers.text: At the festive table {npc} suddenly brings up that broken amphora — in front of everyone, laughing. But {g=npc_sex:his|her} eyes aren't laughing.
ev.y_apple_thrown.title: An apple over the wall
ev.y_apple_thrown.text: An apple came flying over the wall and landed at your feet. Among Greeks that means only one thing: someone is declaring their love. {g:The neighbors' daughter|The neighbors' son} peeks around the corner — and instantly ducks away.
ev.y_apple_thrown.toss_back.success: {g:She|He} caught it and laughed. Ever since that evening you two keep finding reasons to meet at the well.
ev.y_apple_thrown.toss_back.failure: You missed and hit the neighbors' grandmother. And it seems the apple wasn't meant for you at all.
ev.y_apple_thrown.eat: Eat the apple and pretend nothing happened
ev.y_bad_influence.title: Dice at the tavern
ev.y_bad_influence.text: An older youth from the next street, a dandy with a ring on his finger, invites you to the tavern tonight to play dice. 'Stick with me and you'll do fine.'
ev.y_bad_influence.join.success: The dice loved you all evening. You left with full pockets and a ringing head.
ev.y_bad_influence.join.failure: By midnight you'd lost everything you had and still owed more.
ev.y_old_crony.title: An old crony
ev.y_old_crony.text: The dandy you once played dice with has grown older and gone to seed: the ring is long gone. He's up to his ears in debt and asks you to stand surety for him with a moneylender: 'We go way back.'
ev.y_old_crony.vouch.success: To everyone's amazement, he paid on time and now swears you eternal friendship.
ev.y_old_crony.vouch.failure: He vanished from the city, and the moneylender came to you. You had to pay.
ev.y_old_crony.give_coins: Give him a little money — but no surety
ev.y_apprentice_conflict.title: Two weights
ev.y_apprentice_conflict.text: The master you're learning from keeps two weights: an honest one for the market inspector and a light one for customers. He sees that you've understood and winks: 'That's the trade.'
ev.y_apprentice_conflict.confront: Have it out with the master
ev.y_apprentice_conflict.confront.succes: The master was silent a long while, then threw the light weight into the ditch. 'Not a word to anyone,' he muttered.
ev.y_apprentice_conflict.confront.failur: 'Look who's clever,' said the master, and showed you the door.
ev.y_apprentice_conflict.report: Report him to the market inspector
ev.y_honest_name.title: An honest name
ev.y_honest_name.text: The market inspector never forgot how you once exposed the master with the false weight. He recommended you to a wealthy client: 'This one won't cheat you.'
ev.y_slave_broken_vase.title: The broken vase
ev.y_slave_broken_vase.text: The master's son, a boy your age, broke a costly painted vase and ran off in tears. The steward grips his rod: 'Who did it?' From behind a column the boy looks at you pleadingly.
ev.y_slave_broken_vase.silent: Stay silent and stare at the floor
ev.y_young_master_repays.title: The vase remembered
ev.y_young_master_repays.text: The boy you once took a punishment for is now master of the house himself. He calls you in: 'I haven't forgotten the vase. Ask.'
ev.y_young_master_repays.freedom.success: He was silent for a long time, then called for witnesses. You are free.
ev.y_young_master_repays.freedom.failure: 'That I cannot do — my father's will forbids it.' He looked away.
ev.y_young_master_repays.easier: Ask for lighter work and a corner of your own
ev.y_dare.title: A dare
ev.y_dare.text: The kids dare you to spend a night by the old tombs outside the city, where ghosts are said to walk.
ev.y_dare.text.rome: The kids dare you to spend a night among the tombs along the Appian Way, where the lemures — the restless dead — are said to wander.
ev.y_dare.text.athens: The kids dare you to spend a night among the gravestones of the Kerameikos, where Empusa with her donkey's leg is said to prowl.
ev.y_dare.text.egypt: The kids dare you to spend a night in an old tomb at the edge of the desert, where restless spirits are said to wander and jackals howl.
ev.y_dare.accept.success: You sat there until dawn, teeth chattering, but you didn't leave. Now you're a legend of the street.
ev.y_dare.accept.failure: At midnight something rustled, and you bolted for home, banging your knees on a gravestone. In the morning the whole street laughed at you.
ev.y_dare.prank: Go first and scare them instead
ev.y_dare.prank.success: You howled from behind a tomb so horribly that the brave lads scattered, losing their sandals.
ev.y_dare.prank.failure: They recognized your voice, and nobody spoke to you for a week.
ev.y_parents_divorce.title: The divorce
ev.y_parents_divorce.text: Your parents have divorced. By Roman custom the children stay in their father's house, but your mother, leaving for her family's home, whispers: 'Come to me, at least sometimes.' Father has said he won't stand for it.
ev.y_parents_divorce.visit_mother.succes: You see your mother every few days and no one knows. She cries with joy every time.
ev.y_parents_divorce.visit_mother.failur: The slave at the door told your father. There was a terrible row.
ev.y_parents_divorce.plead: Beg your father to let you see her
ev.y_parents_divorce.plead.success: Father frowned for a long time but agreed: on feast days you may go.
ev.y_parents_divorce.plead.failure: 'You belong to this house,' Father snapped.
